questions.short_title: The Four Stages of an IMO Convention, and the Entry-into-Force Delay
questions.text_verbatim: List and explain the four main stages of an IMO convention. With examples, explain the delay that occurs between the adoption date and coming into force date of a convention. What can be done to reduce this delay.

decomposition: The four main stages, named before anything is explained
Stage 1 - proposal and drafting inside the committee structure
Stage 2 - adoption
Stage 3 - acceptance: signature, ratification, accession, approval
Stage 4 - entry into force, and the conditions that trigger it
Why the delay happens - the causes, separated
Worked examples of the delay, stated as they stood at this sitting

reuse_evidence: TIER B - FAMILY. The entry-into-force family is solved five times - QP2506-Q2 (June 2025), QP2508-Q7 (August 2025), QP2511-Q9 (November 2025), QP2602-Q7 (February 2026) and QP2603-Q1 (March 2026) - and all five print the SAME stem as each other: the procedure of entry into force, the provision and its importance, the general conditions for a convention of important technical nature, and definitions of accession and of signature subject to ratification.

It asks for the FOUR MAIN STAGES of a convention, which the family covers only as one part of its procedure limb; for the DELAY between adoption and coming into force WITH EXAMPLES, which the family does not ask for at all; and for WHAT CAN BE DONE TO REDUCE IT, which is an evaluative limb with no counterpart anywhere in the solved corpus. decomposition: The one distinction that organises the whole answer - statutory cycle versus occasional survey
Annual survey
Intermediate survey
Renewal survey
Damage survey
Repair survey
The harmonized system that ties the first three together, and the windows
The statutory certificates - issuing authority and convention
reuse_evidence: TIER C - LIMB-LEVEL REUSE FROM TWO DONORS, neither of which is this question. The stem is a composite of a survey-differentiation task and a certificate-register task.

LIMB (i), SURVEY TYPES: QP2310-Q2 (October 2023, PUSHED NOT INTEGRATED) supplies the purpose of the annual survey, the items examined and condition of class. QP2312-Q8(b) (December 2023) and QP2509-Q9(b) (September 2025), both INTEGRATED, supply the annual-versus-periodical distinction under the harmonized system. QP2503-Q2 and QP2507-Q7 (substantial corrosion at renewal survey) supply renewal-survey depth.

DAMAGE AND REPAIR SURVEYS ARE IN NONE OF THEM AND ARE AUTHORED FRESH. That is not an oversight in the donors - it is the discrimination this examiner is testing. Annual, intermediate and renewal are periodical surveys on a fixed cycle; damage and repair are OCCASIONAL surveys triggered by an event and are not part of the harmonized cycle at all. An answer that lists five surveys as though they were five stages of one cycle has failed the question.

LIMB (ii), CERTIFICATES: QP2406-Q1(a) (June 2024, INTEGRATED) supplies the statutory certificate register with conventions and validity, but is written for an OIL TANKER. This stem asks for the general register, so the tanker-specific entries are marked as such and the general set is extended.
